rv.q: This production is a flamboyant celebration of queerness.
La Barrie nails the heady rush of wealthy excess.
Overall, An Ideal Husband was funny and witty, but it still needs a little more polishing.

cn.t: Wilde's political satire feels remarkably timely in this solid revival, with critics praising its resonant themes of parliamentary corruption, though the production earns moderate rather than enthusiastic acclaim.
